server: graphicle mcp --project . --tools essentials, as graphicle setup writes it for Claude Code (Core)
instructions: When you do not yet know where the code for a task is, who calls it or why it was written that way, call query_graph (the code graph) or recall_project (code, documents and reviewed memory) with the question before searching files by hand; get_node and get_neighbors show one symbol with its callers and callees, and every answer cites file and lines.

tools.name: recall_project
tools.description: Search the project's code, documents, captured agent sessions and reviewed memory together for a question: excerpts cited by path, line and source id within a token budget (max_tokens); read_project_source continues any excerpt, and structured: true returns the whole packet, whose code excerpts carry the stable_id the graph tools cite. Memory is evidence, not permission: no tool can approve memory or run commands.

pack_order.description: chronological presents the selected excerpts by date, with markers where a source's text between two excerpts is not shown; selection stays by rank

reading_guidance.description: add guidance on weighing what users said against what assistants suggested

skip_shown.description: answer excerpts this connection already returned with one-line references and spend their budget on further hits

include.description: search only sources whose id starts with one of these prefixes: file: for the project's files, file:docs/ for a folder, connector:<id>: for one connector's documents

shown.description: source spans already in your context; covered hits return as references

tools.name: read_project_source
tools.description: Read a project file, or a source an answer cited, by path or source id from a byte or line offset: the exact text past an excerpt of recall_project or a graph tool's citation.

snapshot.description: a repository snapshot digest: read a file as that snapshot held it

tools.name: query_graph
tools.description: Find where the code for a question is and how it connects: walks the project's code graph from the functions, classes and files that match the question, with what calls, imports or contains what. The text ends with citations: the code-graph episode read and, for each node it names, its file: path, lines and stable_id (recall_project's structured: true packet carries the same stable_id for the same code); a range not checked against the current file is marked, as is a node reached only through relations read from changed files while their graph is rebuilt. structured: true adds every citation with its byte range in structuredContent. repo names another project, as_of an earlier code graph.

question.description: Natural language question or keyword search

mode.description: bfs=broad context, dfs=trace a specific path

repo.description: The project to read: its id or key, or with graphicle mcp a synced folder. Defaults to this connection's project.

as_of.description: The code-graph episode to read: an episode id, a label such as a commit sha, latest or working. Defaults to the project's current code graph.

tools.name: get_node
tools.description: Find where a function, class or other symbol is defined: its file and line, type, community and number of connections in the project's code graph, by label or id; cited by file: path, lines and stable_id, as query_graph cites.

label.description: Node label or ID to look up

repo.description: The project to read: its id or key, or with graphicle mcp a synced folder. Defaults to this connection's project.

as_of.description: The code-graph episode to read: an episode id, a label such as a commit sha, latest or working. Defaults to the project's current code graph.

tools.name: get_neighbors
tools.description: Find who calls a function or class and what it calls, imports or contains: its direct neighbours in the project's code graph, with each relation; cited by file: path, lines and stable_id, as query_graph cites.

repo.description: The project to read: its id or key, or with graphicle mcp a synced folder. Defaults to this connection's project.

as_of.description: The code-graph episode to read: an episode id, a label such as a commit sha, latest or working. Defaults to the project's current code graph.
